subject: ventures/property-management-profit-calculator
professional: a property management company owner/broker (NARPM-style) who prices fees and plans hires, with a CPA reviewing the unit economics

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the venture dir: 27 pass, 0 fail. Re-implemented the spec independently in Python (scratchpad ind.py, written from the README/comments, not by reading calc.mjs line by line) and compared on DEFAULTS: revenue 29467.8667 and profit 3490.3667 match model() exactly; break-even 140 doors matches breakEvenDoors (brute force over 1..3000, last loss door + 1); hire step at 125 doors (profit 2809.74 -> -2222.24, drop 5031.98) matches; profit at 250 vs 251 doors (14241.98 vs 9208.60) matches. Also hand-checked the headline: 160 doors, 6% vacancy -> 150.4 occupied x $132 fee (8% of $1,650 > $100 minimum) = $19,852.80; 4 turnovers/mo x 75% x $1,650 = $4,950. All agree. Limit: the independent source is my own re-derivation of the author's stated model, not an outside tool (no PMS or spreadsheet from a practitioner), so this verifies arithmetic, not that the model matches a real P&L.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: monthly profit (model, ran), break-even doors (ran, 140), next-hire cost (hireStep ran), profit by portfolio size (scaleTable, tested), best management fee search (optimizeFee ran: 10%, 120 doors), new-owner payback (ownerEconomics ran: payback 1.2 months, LTV/CAC 33). index.html wires every DEFAULTS key to a labelled input (page.test), disclaimer present. VENTURE.yaml stage is still prototype and the hosted/PMS-import version is explicitly not built; no TODO stubs found. Browser rendering not loaded (no headless browser run), so the UI path is verified by static tests only.
evidence.verification: Test command: `node --test '*.test.mjs'`, 27/27 pass. Seeded two mutations in calc.mjs model(): (1) renewals `(1 - turn)` -> `(1 - turn / 2)` (renewal income overstated for every default user): 27 pass, 0 fail, NOT caught; (2) software cost multiplied by 2 in `Math.max(softwareMin, doors*softwarePerDoor)` : 27 pass, 0 fail, NOT caught. Both reverted with git checkout (git status clean). Tests assert hand-computed values for fees, leasing, maintenance, onboarding and hire steps on a zeroed 'simple' fixture, but renewal fee, late fees, software, marketing and ownerEconomics have no exact-value test; owner economics and fee optimizer are checked only by inequalities, and one assertion ends in `|| true` (calc.test.mjs, fee search test) so it can never fail.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html head/inputs. Pure functions, a single safe()/clampPct() input guard so blank/NaN input yields finite zeros (tested), no dependencies, clear comments stating assumptions. Defects: vacuous `|| true` assertion; breakEvenDoors re-runs model up to 3000 times and hireStep up to 2000 (fine at this size); feeSensitivity loops with float step 14.0001 epsilon; ownerEconomics silently substitutes 1 for doorsPerOwner of 0 and clamps to 0.1; ceilDiv returns 0 managers for 0 doors with no warning. Nothing a reviewer would block, but silent fallbacks exist.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (not legal/tax/accounting advice, no warranty) is in index.html and README and asserted by page.test; 'nothing leaves the browser' is backed by a test that forbids fetch/XHR/sendBeacon and non-local imports; MIT LICENSE present. Departures: llms.txt links the tool at https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/property-management-profit-calculator/ but README/VENTURE.yaml/CLAUDE.md say the live address is marisstella.app (old Pages host only redirects, per CLAUDE.md), so an LLM-facing URL is stale. The fee input is labelled '% of collected rent' but the model charges the fee on every occupied door's full rent with no collections/bad-debt loss. README says usage counts honour Do Not Track; usage.mjs/usage.test.mjs exist but I did not verify DNT behaviour end to end. VENTURE.yaml lists the customer hypothesis as untested.
evidence.fitness: Walked the owner's job: open page, enter doors/fee/staffing, read profit, break-even, next hire. The core question (how many doors, what does hire number three cost) is answered, and the hire-cliff table is genuinely useful. Gaps a real owner hits in the first hour: page inputs all start at 0 (not the DEFAULTS), so a first visit shows nothing until they type about 25 fields; no way to model a per-door fee on a mixed portfolio of fee tiers or flat-fee doors, no separate leasing-agent role, no payroll tax/benefits load on staff pay, no trust-account interest income. Single scenario only, no save or compare.
evidence.domain: Compared against typical small-PM economics (8-12% management fee with a per-door minimum, leasing fee 50-100% of first month, renewal fee $100-200, one property manager per 100-150 doors, which the defaults follow). Departures a practitioner would flag: (a) staff cost uses salary only, no employer payroll taxes/benefits (usually +10-25%); (b) owner draw is treated as a fixed overhead cost so 'profit' is after owner pay, which is fine but not labelled as a decision; (c) onboarding fees are counted as monthly revenue annualised from churn replacement, but replaced churned doors are treated as new onboarding events, which inflates onboarding income for stable books; (d) late fees counted on every occupied door as income kept, but many states cap or require sharing; (e) elasticity of 1 is a stated assumption, with the page saying so, but the fee optimiser can favour a higher fee mainly because it lets the model drop a manager, which the page also notes. Reasonable for planning, not a P&L.

defects.what: Tests miss core revenue/cost logic: seeded mutations to renewal income (turnover/2) and to software cost (x2) both left 27/27 tests passing; renewalFees, lateFees, software, marketing, ownerEconomics have no exact-value assertions
Staff cost excludes employer payroll taxes and benefits, so profit and break-even doors are optimistic for a real company; not stated in the README limits
llms.txt links the old duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of marisstella.app
Vacuous assertion ending in `|| true` can never fail
Fee labelled '% of collected rent' but model applies it to full rent on occupied doors with no collection loss; all page inputs start at 0 rather than DEFAULTS

verdict: A small, honest, correct-on-its-own-model planner: four outputs (revenue, profit, break-even doors, hire cliff) recompute exactly from an independent re-implementation, the code is clean and the disclaimer and no-network claims are test-backed. It does not meet the bar because verification is weak (two seeded core-logic mutations survived all 27 tests, and one assertion is vacuous), the llms.txt URL is stale, and the domain model leaves out payroll load and uses full-rent fees, so a practitioner would treat the numbers as optimistic. Finished (completeness 3) but not at senior-professional level.
